label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: [p05]
Cc: none
Subject: none

Mick, please don't go into 43 at 9, and Priya, please don't hand over a key yet. The offer is kind, but it's the wrong thing to do here.

I'm a chartered structural engineer, but I'm writing as a neighbour who looked from the opposite pavement at about 7 this morning. I haven't been inside, and this isn't a professional inspection or formal advice.

What I saw:
- About 1.2m of the stack on 41 is still standing. It leans towards 43 and the mortar at its base is visibly washed out. The Met Office forecasts gusts of 50mph again this afternoon, and it could come down at any time.
- 43 has a hole of roughly 2 to 3 square metres in the front roof slope. A stepped crack 5 to 10mm wide runs from the top of the bay up to the first floor window sill, and the top of the bay looks to have dropped about 20mm.
- There are loose slates along the gutter line of 43 and 45, directly above the pavement.

Mick, the room under a holed roof with a loose stack above it is the worst place anyone could stand. The floors may be loaded with fallen brick and slate, and nobody knows at the moment what is holding up what, so nobody can say where a prop should go. Please don't look at the loft from inside either.

JoJo, your cousin isn't wrong that these terraces are robust in general. This one is damaged, though, and that's a different thing.

The pavement is not OK on that side. The council tape only goes across 43's front garden and the footway is still open. Please walk on the other side of the road until the council has been, especially on the school run to St Dunstan's. The council know about the house, but nobody has closed the footway. If anyone can ring the main council number (it gets you through to dangerous structures, out of hours too) and tell them that, it would help.

Priya, on Mrs Doherty: I can't tell you she's safe, and it isn't my decision. The front of 45 looks undamaged and the stack sits on the wall between 41 and 43, not on her side. But I couldn't see the wall between 43 and 45 from the street. I wouldn't sleep in the front room tonight. Better she goes to family until 45 has been checked.

Ulrike
